newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian court acquits reporters on security charges.
newsitem.headline: Zambian court acquits reporters on security charges.

text.p: A Zambian court on Thursday dismissed a case which could have seen three journalists with an independent daily imprisoned for up to 25 years under the country's security laws.

The Lusaka High Court found the Post editor Fred M'membe and reporters Masautso Phiri and Bright Mwape not guilty on charges of contravening the State Security Act by publishing classified information.
Judge Peter Chitengi said the reports in no way threatened the security of the state.
"Not all information classified by an authorised official falls under the ambit of the State Security Act," Chitengi said.
"The act was intended to deal with serious matters such as espionage or sabotage -- matters that subvert the interests of the state," he added.

Police arrested the three journalists in February after Zambian President Frederick Chiluba banned an issue of the Post which claimed the government planned to hold a referendum on a new constitution. Chiluba said the report breached the country's security laws.
Chitengi said: "A referendum is no more than an election and an election cannot be a state secret in these days of transparency. For this reason, I must rule that the accused have no case to answer".
Early this year three other Zambian journalists were arrested by the police in separate cases in what was widely seen as a government clampdown on the independent press.
The government shelved plans to establish a state-controlled media council to regulate journalists in response to diplomatic pressure.
